# Gamma-phi flash with an NRTL liquid

`eos.ge_nrtl_flash`

## Source

**NeqSim master `SystemEosGE`**

the gamma-phi branch of `TPflash`, `sucsSubsGammaPhi`, whose K update is `phi_i^L / phi_i^V` with `presdiff` one because both phases are at the feed's pressure.

DOI: [10.1016/0378-3812(82)85001-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-3812(82)85001-2)


## Algorithm

A model rather than a calculation: what this page pins down is the procedure,
not an equation, and both implementations read it from here.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Scheme | `successive_substitution_flash` |
| Convergence | `absolute` |
| Tolerance | `1e-10` |
| Max iterations | `300` |
| Initialisation | `wilson` |

## Inner procedure

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Scheme | `rachford_rice_bisection` |
| Convergence | `absolute` |
| Tolerance | `1e-14` |
| Max iterations | `200` |

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `components` | - | the substances the mixture is made of, by name. The NRTL matrices and each component's Antoine correlation resolve against the databank, and the cubic resolves `Tc`, `Pc`, `omega` and the `kij` pairs for the vapour. |
| `T` | K | absolute temperature |
| `P` | Pa | absolute pressure |
| `z` | dimensionless | overall mole fractions. Checked rather than renormalised: the entries must be non-negative and sum to one to within a tolerance. |
| `eos` | pr / srk / rk / tst | *Optional.* the cubic the vapour is. A gamma-phi flash is defined by the pair, so the cubic is part of the model rather than the caller's convenience: NeqSim pairs SRK with its activity models and the cases are stated against it, and any other member is a different vapour from the same liquid. |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `beta` | dimensionless | *Optional.* The vapour fraction, in `[0, 1]` for a two-phase split; outside that it is the negative-flash value and the feed is single phase. Absent where there is genuinely no vapour fraction. |
| `x` | dimensionless | liquid-phase mole fractions |
| `y` | dimensionless | vapour-phase mole fractions |
| `k` | dimensionless | K-values, `K_i = y_i / x_i = phi_i^L / phi_i^V`, the iterate the loop converges on. |
| `ln_phi_liquid` | dimensionless | the liquid's fugacity coefficients as logarithms, `ln(gamma_i P0_i / P)`, from the NRTL phase. |
| `ln_phi_vapour` | dimensionless | the vapour's fugacity coefficients as logarithms, from the cubic at the vapour composition. |
| `z_vapour` | dimensionless | the vapour root of the cubic at the vapour composition, the largest admissible one. There is no liquid root: the liquid is not a cubic and has no compressibility factor. |
| `min_t_over_tc` | dimensionless | the smallest `T / Tc_i` over the components - how close the mixture is to the nearest component's critical point. A cubic's vapour is what it is reading. |
| `phase` | two_phase / all_liquid / all_vapour / trivial | What the converged state is: `two_phase` (`beta` in `[0, 1]`), `all_liquid`, `all_vapour`, or `trivial` (the iteration converged to `x = y = z`). |
| `iterations` | dimensionless | successive-substitution steps taken, including the final evaluation of the converged state. |
| `residual` | dimensionless | `rms_i |ln K_i - ln K_i_previous|` at the last step the loop completed. NaN when no step completed. |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `T > 0` | raises | an absolute temperature; zero and below are not states |
| `P > 0` | raises | an absolute pressure; zero and below are not states. The vapour cubic needs a positive `B`, and the phase needs a positive divisor for `gamma_i P0_i / P`. |

## Assumptions

- the vapour is a cubic and the liquid is an activity-coefficient phase. This is NeqSim's `SystemEosGE` pairing: `SystemNRTL` builds `PhaseSrkEos` into slot 0 and `PhaseGENRTL` into slot 1, and the K-value the flash iterates is `phi_i^L / phi_i^V`.
- the cubic is part of the model rather than the caller's convenience: a gamma-phi flash is defined by the pair. NeqSim pairs SRK with its activity models, and the cases are stated against it.
- `K_i = gamma_i P0_i / (phi_i^V P)`, i.e. `y_i phi_i^V P = x_i gamma_i P0_i`. The liquid's `phi_i^L` is `eos.ge_nrtl_phase`'s and the vapour's is the cubic's, neither recomputed here. A component tagged a Henry's-law solute is refused by that phase, and this model inherits the refusal.
- `P0_i` has no Poynting correction: the liquid's fugacity is `gamma_i x_i P0_i` and nothing else. At the pressures an activity model is used at the term is small, but it is absent rather than neglected quietly.
- no stability test: successive substitution finds a stationary point of the flash equations, and which single phase a `trivial` feed is cannot be answered by this model.
- no damping and no acceleration: plain successive substitution. NeqSim's one direct gamma-phi system damps its K-value updates and clamps one component's, both of which are empirical tuning of that system rather than of the method.
- Wilson K-values open the iteration. They are a cubic's estimate and are used only as a starting point - the loop's residual is measured on the gamma-phi K-values it then computes.
- the two phases are at the same temperature and pressure as the feed - a flash, not a rigorous column stage. Nothing here does an energy balance.
- the Antoine correlations the phase reads are the databank's, evaluated at the state's temperature. A component the databank carries no correlation for has no `P0` and is refused by `eos.ge_nrtl_phase` before this iteration starts.
